column1: MOCK DATA: rehearsal Budget for PolicyEngine drill 4
column2: 19 October 2026. Not a real Budget. Skip one line when reading this CSV.

column13: reason

Existing pe-uk thresholds: add 2031-04-06 range values for the Personal Allowance, basic rate limit, NICs thresholds and the Secondary Threshold. The engine's counterfactual indexes by its own September 2030 CPI, not the Annex A value; income tax is 90% cash.
Corporation tax on banks: business-side, no household representation.

No live parameter: the contrib pensioner allowance is read by no formula and the State Pension is hard-coded into taxable income. Needs a modifier (or upstream variable) computing the allowance, its rounding and its pound-for-pound withdrawal.

column12: trap: the £150 core rebate is baseline, not part of the measure
column13: No Warm Home Discount variable in the engine: the drill's pre-built upstream variable (P8) or a dashboard lump-sum modifier keyed to benefit receipt on the qualifying date, England and Wales only; the data has no receipt or named-on-bill flag.
Range keys on the fuel duty rate (day-weighted on 2.130.1). The costing covers all road fuel, households and businesses; the engine covers household fuel only. Duty only; cash one month behind.

column12: trap: a VAT line that reads like a household tax
column13: A collection mechanism on marketplaces; the yield is reduced non-compliance by sellers, with no household tax-benefit representation.

Existing starting-rate-for-savings parameter, but the engine's savings_starter_rate_income starts the band taper at Personal Allowance + £5,000 of already-taxable non-savings income (ITA 2007 s.12 reduces the band by all taxable non-savings income), so the band is too generous in the baseline and the reform. Key holder found this with a policyengine-uk 2.125.1 spot check (local clone of 23 Sep shows the same formula); file it at the debrief. Savings interest is also under-recorded in survey data, and half the yield is cash a year later.

Existing CGT higher-rate parameters (and the residential property rate). Gains are imputed, and the forward path, forestalling and realisations response are outside a static run; receipts are cash, mostly a year later.
Business rates are paid by businesses.
Business rates relief for businesses.

LHA freeze and percentile parameters; holding rates at the April 2027 level after a one-off reset may need a structural tweak or upstream parameter. Gaps come from take-up and caseload; Great Britain only.

column12: trap: employer-side, so the static household change is £0
column13: No under-21 or age-band employer parameter in the engine: an age-band modifier on employer NICs. Compare gross employer NICs with the static costing; the post-behavioural figure is net of pass-through.
A duty on gaming machine operators' profits.
Existing UC child element parameters. The costing uses a full-entitlement caseload; the engine applies modelled take-up.

column12: trap: computable parameters exist, but the drill dataset (Microcosm national 04a496f2) has no alcohol volume inputs, so any run scores £0
column13: Alcohol duty parameters exist, but Microcosm national (04a496f2) has no alcohol volume inputs (only alcohol_and_tobacco_consumption), as the enhanced FRS did not; the national figure must be published as not computable, never £0.
Compliance yield has no household tax-benefit representation.

Unanticipated: no age-based Child Benefit supplement exists in the engine; needs a new variable (or a fallback modifier) that also feeds the High Income Child Benefit Charge. The costing is net of the charge.
No fuel-specific VAT rate in the engine (VAT is a generic share of consumption): a modifier on petrol and diesel spending with day-weighting over a window crossing financial years.
A levy on oil and gas producers' profits.

column12: trap: Scotland (LBTT) and Wales (LTT) are unaffected
column13: Microcosm national (04a496f2) has no additional_residential_property_purchased input, so the engine computes nil higher-rates SDLT in baseline and reform: the binding constraint is a missing input (route data; publish as not computable nationally). The engine's additional-dwelling rates are also stale (pre-2024 surcharge), a parameter fix upstream. The household case is computable by hand. England and Northern Ireland only.

column12: trap: Scottish carers receive Carer Support Payment, which this measure does not change
column13: Existing earnings-limit parameter, but the engine applies Carer's Allowance rules in Scotland too; the Scottish exclusion needs a structural tweak or is a devolved gap.

column12: trap: reads like a household CGT change
column13: Microcosm national (04a496f2) carries capital_gains_badr, but no reinvestment, holding or disposal-type data, so the relief is still not computable; narrative row citing the costing.
No inheritance tax in the engine and no estate data.
Departmental spending.
An equity loan (a financial transaction) with a subsidy cost; not a tax-benefit transfer.
Devolution of revenues and a local levy power; capacity funding is departmental spending.

column12: trap: sits with young workers but is a payment to employers
column13: Payments to employers and training places; departmental spending.
A levy on producers and importers of soft drinks; the engine has no soft drinks spending or levy.
